items.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So that was kind of my – not rude awakening – but let me know that I don't want to go through this kind of conversation with this guy. We've gotta play two more weeks together.

ctx.x: I don't want to spend a lot of time on that, but really … I guess that was my first real … real … um … real … determining factor on how I felt, how valid my view was on music. Knowing the challenge, what I did up to this point, nobody said, "That's not gonna work." I mean, I played in Miles' band which was The band of the times, I played with Cannonball on a tour, I had a pretty good musical CV behind me, and this guy's telling me that my notes don't work, he's not gonna do it. I said, "What!?" "No, you're gonna…
The story floored me just because of your personality, that you were ready to fight.
